kept.title: Cache native CDOs and classes in cdo(): every StaticFindObject is a ~3 ms GUObjectArray walk on this UE4SS (the whole 'clock' part)
kept.where: sv_ai.lua:1062 cdo() calls StaticFindObject on every call; sv_ai.lua:1064-1070 toText() calls cdo(KismetTextLibrary) for every SetText. sv_spawn.lua:6-17 gameClock()/gamePaused() each call cdo(GameplayStatics). sv_flights.lua:393-405 roundClock() calls both every tick, timed as 'clock' at sv_main.lua:544-547. sv_coop.lua:4530-4559 COOP.tick calls gamePaused + cdo + gameClock every tick while peers are linked (3 more lookups). Raw StaticFindObject('/Script/...') calls on hot or per-object paths: sv_shop.lua:73 (UMG.Image, every 0.5 s at the airfield), sv_rounds.lua:254 (GameplayStatics for each object a special's clean-up finishes off), sv_ladon.lua:42 (for each Ladon part), sv_coop.lua:929 (for each copy killed)
kept.perf_part: clock 6.3/15 (26%) solo round 1, 6.8/13 Alicorn. Part of hud 2.2 (steady ~0.5 ms; the rest is the 416 ms HUD build). coop 9.9/25 on the 0.73.70 hosts (that build's untimed 8.6 ms held clock, rows watch and info maps)
kept.frequency: Every tick (clock: 2 lookups). Every tick with co-op peers linked (+3). Once per changed HUD text (the countdown changes each second) and once per STORE/menu relabel row. Every 0.5 s at the airfield. Once per object in a special's clean-up or a Ladon parts kill
kept.cost: UE4SS.log of both 2026-11-03 sessions says '[PS] Failed to find FUObjectHashTables::Get()' and '[HashTables] FUObjectHashTables unavailable, object lookups use GUObjectArray', so StaticFindObject searches the whole object array by name. The 'clock' part makes only 2 StaticFindObject, 2 ProcessEvent (GetTimeSeconds, IsGamePaused) and 3 IsValid calls, yet averages 6.3 ms a tick with a 15 ms worst. A plane-sweep visit (~15-25 UObject calls) costs ~0.4 ms, so ProcessEvent is not the cost: each StaticFindObject is ~3 ms on Saint Alessia's PC, and the cost grows with the object count. Total: ~6.5 ms a tick solo, ~15 ms a tick in co-op with peers linked, 3 ms per HUD or STORE label change (a STORE press that relabels 6 rows is ~18 ms), and N x 3 ms hitches in clean-ups
kept.fix: In sv_ai.lua keep a cache: `local CDO_CACHE = {}; function cdo(path) local o = CDO_CACHE[path]; if o ~= nil and liveObj(o) then return o end; o = StaticFindObject(path); if valid(o) then CDO_CACHE[path] = o; return o end; CDO_CACHE[path] = nil; return nil end`. Use it only for '/Script/...' paths: native class objects and their CDOs are created at startup and never collected. toText, gameClock and gamePaused then cost no lookup. Replace the raw StaticFindObject('/Script/...') calls listed above (and sv_coop.lua:433, sv_rounds.lua:99/117, sv_anomalies' Niagara/Kismet/Engine class lookups) with cdo(). Optional: pass roundClock's t (bNow) to COOP.tick's world-clock check instead of a third GetTimeSeconds
kept.gameplay_note: The same objects and calls, found once instead of every time
kept.risk: Very low. Native CDOs and UClasses never unload, and liveObj (SV_ObjChain, GUObjectArray only) still guards each reuse. Never cache '/Game/' blueprint CDOs (sv_alicorn.lua:175, sv_anomalies.lua:809/846): they can unload and their address can be reused

verify.cost_check: sv_ai.lua:1062 `function cdo(path) local o = StaticFindObject(path); return valid(o) and o or nil end` has no cache. roundClock (sv_flights.lua:393-405) runs every tick inside the timed 'clock' part (sv_main.lua:544-547). It calls gameClock (sv_spawn.lua:6 `cdo("/Script/Engine.Default__GameplayStatics")`) and, whenever the clock moved, gamePaused (another cdo). So the part is 2 StaticFindObject + 2 ProcessEvent + IsValid, and it averages 6.3 ms/tick (6.8 in the Alicorn minute). That fits '[HashTables] FUObjectHashTables unavailable, object lookups use GUObjectArray' (UE4SS.log line 622/623, both sessions). Cross-check: info maps (1 SFO + 1 FindRow + reads) is ~7 ms a call and rows watch (2 SFO + ~6 FindRow) ~14 ms a pass, so ~3 ms per lookup holds up. With peers linked, COOP.tick (sv_coop.lua:4530-4559) does gamePaused, then cdo + gameClock: 3 more each tick. toText (sv_ai.lua:1064) does a cdo per changed HUD/STORE/menu label, and setText is change-gated (sv_hud.lua:216-220), so about 1/s for the countdown. Overstated: sv_rounds.lua:254, sv_ladon.lua:42 and sv_coop.lua:929 look up only when ModifyHealth left health > 0, which is rare, and sv_coop.lua:433 already caches planeCls. Missed and worth adding: newWidget (sv_ai.lua:1074) does StaticFindObject('/Script/UMG.'..cls) for every widget, and the log shows 87 widgets per HUD build ('hud: built ... 87 widgets'). At ~3 ms each that is roughly 260 ms of the 416 ms 'hud' worst. Every current cdo() caller passes a '/Script/...' path (grep).
verify.gameplay_check: None. The same native CDOs and UClasses are used and the same calls are made. HUD text, the clock and pause detection behave identically.
verify.safety_check: Native CDOs and UClasses are rooted and never collected or unloaded, so a cached wrapper stays valid for the whole session. Re-checking with liveObj (SV_ObjChain, GUObjectArray only) on each reuse is cheap belt-and-braces. Only '/Script/' paths may be cached: assert the prefix inside the cache and fall through to a plain StaticFindObject otherwise, so a later caller passing a '/Game/' BP CDO (sv_alicorn.lua:175, sv_anomalies.lua:809/846) is never cached. A nil result is not cached. The cache is one table, adds no locals in hot chunks, and is untouched by teardown.
verify.refined_fix: In sv_ai.lua: `local CDO_C = {}; function cdo(path) local o = CDO_C[path]; if o ~= nil and liveObj(o) then return o end; o = StaticFindObject(path); if valid(o) then if path:sub(1,8) == '/Script/' then CDO_C[path] = o end; return o end; CDO_C[path] = nil; return nil end`. newWidget then uses `local c = cdo('/Script/UMG.' .. cls)`. Route the raw '/Script/...' lookups through cdo(): sv_shop.lua:73 (UMG.Image, every 0.5 s on the airfield), sv_rounds.lua:99/117/242/254, sv_ladon.lua:42, sv_coop.lua:929, sv_main.lua:935/948/954, sv_core.lua:139 (loadObject's KismetSystemLibrary), sv_down.lua's component classes, and sv_anomalies' /Script lookups. Optionally COOP.tick can reuse probeTick's game time for its world-clock check instead of a third GetTimeSeconds. It runs in the same half, right after probeTick, but bNow/bPaused are file-locals of sv_main.lua, so expose them as a global first.
verify.est_saving: ~6 ms every tick solo (clock 6.3 -> ~0.2), plus ~9 ms a tick in co-op with peers linked, ~0.5-0.75 ms a tick of HUD label changes, ~3 ms off each airfield decor pass, and ~250 ms off each HUD build (416 ms worst -> ~150)

kept.title: Rows watch: 2 StaticFindObject, 4 GetFullName and ~6 FindRow every second during a run, for menu tables nothing reads in a run
kept.where: sv_main.lua:903-908 runs watchRows every 4th tick (first half) for the whole session. sv_core.lua:691-751 watchRows, per table: :696 StaticFindObject(t.game); :713 pin(game, nameOf(game)), which does a GetFullName even when the table is already pinned, plus nameOf at :704; :714 hideRows, one FindRow per hidden row (CampaignTraining, Shop, Online in the logs); putRow, one FindRow per row. sv_flights.lua:473-486 shopRowsTick: once the rows are in, every 4 s it still calls loadObject(SHOP.game) (StaticFindObject first) and inSurvival(pc) (GetFullName) before `if SH.added then return`
kept.perf_part: rows watch 3.5/18 (15%) solo, 3.1/16 Alicorn. shop rows 2.0/84 and 1.7/87 (first minute, includes the initial add)
kept.frequency: Once a second (rows watch), every 4 s (shop rows), in every run
kept.cost: About 14 ms per pass (3.5 ms a tick x 4), worst 18: one frame missed every second in flight. shop rows about 3-4 ms every 4 s (~0.2 ms a tick) once the rows are in
kept.fix: (1) sv_main.lua:904: `if not rowsStopped and ((tick % 4 == 0 and (D == nil or tick % 240 == 0)) or not (ready[1] and ready[2]))`, so the watch runs 1/s at the menus and once a minute in a run. (2) watchRows: keep each table's object (t.obj) and reuse it while liveObj(t.obj); call StaticFindObject/loadObject only when it's gone. Call pin()/nameOf only when the address changed. Skip hideRows while D. (3) shopRowsTick: keep SH.gameObj, and return first thing when SH.added and liveObj(SH.gameObj) and liveObj(survivalPC)
kept.gameplay_note: DT_LiveMenuMainTopCommands and the mission row are read only at the main menu and the hangar. Both tables are pinned in GameInstance.ReferencedObjects, so they can't be collected and reloaded during a run. The watch is back to 1/s as soon as D is nil
kept.risk: Low. Another mod that removes or reorders main-menu rows during a run is repaired up to 60 s later, and at once at the main menu

verify.cost_check: sv_main.lua:903 `if not rowsStopped and (tick % 4 == 0 or not (ready[1] and ready[2]))` runs watchRows once a second for the whole session. Per pass, watchRows (sv_core.lua:691-751) does: `local game = StaticFindObject(t.game)` for both tables (2 SFO, ~6 ms); `pin(game, nameOf(game))`, where the nameOf argument (SV_ObjChain + GetFullName) is evaluated even though pin() returns at once when `pinned[a] ~= nil` (2 GetFullName, not 4 as claimed); hideRows on the menu table (4 FindRow: CampaignTraining prepended plus CFG.menu.hide {Shop, Online, CampaignTraining}); and putRow (one FindRow per wanted row). Measured: rows watch 3.5/18 ms a tick = ~14 ms per pass. shopRowsTick (sv_flights.lua:473-486), every 16 ticks: liveObj(survivalPC), `inSurvival(pc)` (GetFullName), then `loadObject(SHOP.game)` (StaticFindObject first), and only then `if SH.added then return end`. That is ~3-4 ms every 4 s once the rows are in. The logs show both tables pinned ('... pinned (kept loaded) [ReferencedObjects num 0 -> 1 ...]').
verify.gameplay_check: None in a run. Both tables are pinned, so they can't be collected and reloaded, and the game only reads them at the main menu and the hangar. Back at the menus (D nil) the watch runs every second as now. The only delay is when another mod removes main-menu rows mid-run: that would be repaired up to 60 s later, or as soon as the run ends.
verify.safety_check: Keeping the table objects between ticks needs liveObj(t.obj) before each use, with a fresh StaticFindObject/loadObject when one is gone (they are pinned, so this should never fire). Proposed shopRowsTick fast path: SH.added and liveObj(SH.gameObj) and liveObj(survivalPC), skipping inSurvival. That is unsafe as worded. survivalPC is never cleared after the level is left (it is only reset at the next level load, sv_main.lua:452), so a reused address could pass liveObj and skip taking the shop rows out of stock missions' landing table. Guard the fast path with svLevelOn (sv_config.lua's world watch) and with survivalPC's address as verified by inSurvival. Gate in-run work on D only, never on rowsStopped.
verify.refined_fix: (1) watchRows: keep t.obj, reuse it while liveObj(t.obj), and call StaticFindObject/loadObject only when it is gone. Call nameOf/pin/log only when addrOf(game) differs from seen[i]. Call hideRows only when D == nil or the address changed. (2) Cadence in sv_main.lua: `if not rowsStopped and ((tick % 4 == 0 and (D == nil or tick % 120 == 0)) or not (ready[1] and ready[2]))`, i.e. 1/s at the menus and every 30 s in a run. The pass is now ~2 FindRow, so even 1/s would be fine. (3) shopRowsTick: when the full path verifies inSurvival(pc), store SH.gameObj = game and SH.pcAddr = addrOf(pc). At the top add `if SH.added and svLevelOn and SH.gameObj and liveObj(SH.gameObj) and survivalPC and addrOf(survivalPC) == SH.pcAddr and liveObj(survivalPC) then return end`. Otherwise run the existing path unchanged, including the removal branch.
verify.est_saving: ~3.4 ms a tick in a run (rows watch 3.5 -> ~0.1, a 14-18 ms first-half spike every second gone), plus ~0.2 ms a tick from shop rows (a 3-4 ms spike every 4 s)

kept.title: Info maps: a StaticFindObject and a mission-row FindRow every 2 s, used only when a key is missing
kept.where: sv_main.lua:909-912 calls infoMapsTick every 8th tick. sv_core.lua:775-802 infoMapsTick: :777 gameInstance(), :779 gi.InformationManager_, :781 StaticFindObject(TABLES[1].game) and :783 FindRow(ROW) run on every call before the maps are checked. has() at :763-773 uses map:Contains, or a ForEach over the whole map when this UE4SS has no Contains
kept.perf_part: info maps 0.9/9 (4%) solo, 0.8/8 Alicorn
kept.frequency: Every 2 s for the whole session, runs included
kept.cost: About 7 ms per call (0.9 x 8), worst 9: 1 StaticFindObject (~3 ms), a FindRow of Survival's mission row, 2 property reads, 2 map lookups (or 2 full ForEach walks)
kept.fix: Check has(map, m.ours) first. Read src/row only when a key is missing; they are unused otherwise. Keep src as the pinned table object (liveObj) instead of StaticFindObject. In sv_main.lua run it every 2 s only while D == nil (main menu, hangar) and every 60 s in a run. The steady pass is then 1 property read + 2 Contains
kept.gameplay_note: MissionDataMap_/LevelDataMap_ are read by the hangar and at sortie, which happen in other levels before D exists
kept.risk: Low. Same repair, decided later in a run

verify.cost_check: sv_main.lua:909 `if tick % 8 == 2 then timed("info maps", infoMapsTick)`, for the whole session. infoMapsTick (sv_core.lua:775-802) runs `local _, src = pcall(function() return StaticFindObject(TABLES[1].game) end)` and `dtCall(src, "FindRow", ROW)` on every call, before the loop that does `if has(map, m.ours) then ... return end`. The logs show Contains works ('info maps: MissionDataMap_ has 9101' at 13:17:02 and 13:34:58, after the start race was fixed at 13:17:00/13:34:55), so the steady pass is 1 SFO (~3 ms) + 1 FindRow + 2 property reads + 2 Contains. verify.gameplay_check: None. The repair (adding 9101 / 70 when missing) is unchanged, and the row is still read in the same pass whenever a key is missing. The maps are read by the hangar and at sortie, in other levels.
verify.safety_check: Reordering is pure logic. If src is kept between ticks (e.g. reusing finding 1's pinned t.obj), check liveObj before FindRow. gameInstance() already liveObj-checks GI.obj, and the im read is pcall'd and valid()-checked as now. Cutting the cadence in a run is optional: once the pass is cheap, keeping 2 s everywhere avoids any doubt about a mid-run rebuild of the maps (e.g. a pause-menu restart).
verify.refined_fix: In infoMapsTick, read gi.InformationManager_, then for each map check `has(map, m.ours)` and `has(map, m.stock)` first. Only when a map is missing its key (with the stock key present), get src (finding 1's kept TABLES[1] object if liveObj, else StaticFindObject) and FindRow(ROW), once per pass, lazily. Keep the 2 s cadence, or 2 s while D == nil and 30 s in a run.
verify.est_saving: ~0.85 ms a tick (a 7-9 ms spike every 2 s becomes ~0.2 ms)

kept.title: At the airfield, landingWindows() walks every object (35-71 ms) twice a second, solo and co-op; the ammo panel walks too
kept.where: sv_core.lua:107-124 landingWindows(): FindAllOf('WBP_Menu_IngameHangar_Common_000_C') the first time it's asked in a tick. Callers: sv_shop.lua:71-80 SHOP.decorTick on every even tick while playerOnAirfield() (within 3 km and under 100 m of the runway, or whenever the pawn can't be read, sv_rounds.lua:1087), and sv_main.lua:567 (co-op music hold, even ticks). sv_main.lua:81-89 hangarAmmoTick: FindAllOf('WBP_Menu_IngameHangar_WeaponDetail_002_C') every 8-32 ticks. sv_main.lua:45 slotTexts: FindAllOf('TextBlock') plus nameOf (GetFullName) on every TextBlock, up to 3 tries per new panel
kept.perf_part: icons / ammo panel / shop / music hold. 0.73.70 co-op logs: icons up to 2.9 ms a tick averaged over 5 min (worst 13-47), ammo panel worst 54-112, shop worst 100-286. Not measured on 0.73.78: Saint Alessia didn't land inside the perf minute
kept.frequency: Twice a second whenever you're on the ground at the airfield (landing roll, taxi, STORE, takeoff roll), solo and co-op
kept.cost: Each walk covers the whole object array: 35-71 ms on Saint Alessia's PC (her 'walks:' line). That is a 2-4 frame hitch every 0.5 s, ~17-35 ms a tick on average while landed, plus decorTick's UMG.Image StaticFindObject (~3 ms) each pass. The TextBlock walk adds a GetFullName per TextBlock (thousands)
kept.fix: Feed the windows from construction. In sv_core.lua: `pcall(NotifyOnNewObject, '/Script/Live.LiveMenuIngameHangarWidget', function(o) LW.fed[#LW.fed+1] = o end)`. That is the native class of the window and the landing pages (docs/re/AIRFIELD_SHOP_UI.md 1.2); the callback only records, like the LiveAIPlane notify. landingWindows() then filters LW.fed with liveObj, liveWidget and the class name 'WBP_Menu_IngameHangar_Common_000_C' (the verdict cached per address), drops dead entries, and falls back to the FindAllOf at most once per landing if nothing was fed this level. LEVEL_DROPS clears LW.fed. hangarAmmoTick: read each window's reflected child WBP_Menu_IngameHangar_WeaponDetail_002 (childWidget) instead of its FindAllOf. For the slot TextBlocks, walk down the panel's WidgetTree (RootWidget, GetChildrenCount/GetChildAt, as hudDump does at sv_spawn.lua:46-67) instead of FindAllOf('TextBlock')
kept.gameplay_note: The same windows and panels, found without walking every object. Icons, labels, the ammo caps display and the co-op music hold are unchanged
kept.risk: Low to medium. UE4SS's NotifyOnNewObject needs a loaded native class (pcall it and keep the walk as fallback). A STORE page whose window isn't a LiveMenuIngameHangarWidget would need the fallback walk. The WidgetTree descent for the ammo slots needs a test (GetWidgetFromName read nil there in the 2026-10-23 test)

verify.cost_check: SHOP.decorTick (sv_shop.lua:71-80), called from probeTickB as timed 'icons': `if not CFG.shop.enabled or tick % 2 ~= 0 or not playerOnAirfield() then return end; local imgClass = StaticFindObject("/Script/UMG.Image") ... for _, win in ipairs(landingWindows(tick))`. landingWindows (sv_core.lua:107-124) caches per tick only (`if LW.tick == tick and LW.list then return LW.list end`) and otherwise does `FindAllOf("WBP_Menu_IngameHangar_Common_000_C")`. That is one full-object walk every even tick (0.5 s) whenever playerOnAirfield() holds: within 3 km and under 100 m of the runway, or no readable location (sv_rounds.lua:1085-1091). It holds through the landing roll, taxi, STORE and takeoff roll, whether or not a landing menu is open. In co-op the music hold (sv_main.lua:567) makes the walk on the same tick, and the half-B call reuses it (same tick value). Walks cost 35-71 ms on Saint Alessia's PC ('walks:' line). hangarAmmoTick walks WeaponDetail_002_C only every 8 s or on a window change (tick%8==1 with a new key, tick%32==1). slotTexts' TextBlock walk is at most 3 tries per new panel, 2 s apart. Not measured on 0.73.78 (she didn't land inside the perf minute). The 0.73.70 logs show icons worst 13-47 ms and ammo panel worst 54-112.
verify.gameplay_check: None if the fed list finds the same windows: the icons, labels, ammo caps and co-op music hold are unchanged. The only possible difference is a window the notify misses, which a fallback walk must cover.
verify.safety_check: The NotifyOnNewObject callback must only record (like the LiveAIPlane, LiveMenuManager and LiveMissile notifies). Each read filters with liveObj then nameOf, requiring the name to start with 'WBP_Menu_IngameHangar_Common_000_C ' and contain '/Engine/Transient' (liveWidget). Do NOT cache a per-address 'is a window' verdict: an address freed and reused passes liveObj, so the name check must be repeated (a few GetFullName on a short list are cheap). Prune dead entries on each read, cap the list (e.g. 256), and clear it in LEVEL_DROPS (add LW.fed and LW.list to a LEVEL_DROPS entry) and at level load. Keep walkHold semantics: a held read returns {}. If pcall(NotifyOnNewObject, '/Script/Live.LiveMenuIngameHangarWidget', ...) fails, keep today's walk. The STORE pages and the Confirmation shells are also LiveMenuIngameHangarWidget subclasses (AIRFIELD_SHOP_UI.md 1.2), so the name filter must keep only Common_000 windows. The WidgetTree descent for the ammo slots is untested (GetWidgetFromName read nil inside the panel on 2026-10-23), so keep slotTexts' walk as its fallback.
verify.refined_fix: sv_core.lua: `LW.fed = {}; LW.notify = pcall(NotifyOnNewObject, '/Script/Live.LiveMenuIngameHangarWidget', function(o) if #LW.fed < 256 then LW.fed[#LW.fed+1] = o end end)`. In landingWindows, when LW.notify: build `out` from LW.fed, dropping entries that fail liveObj and keeping those that pass liveWidget plus the Common_000 name test, with no FindAllOf. Validation: do one FindAllOf per level, the first time playerOnAirfield() is true for 5 s. If it finds a live window the fed list lacks, log it and set LW.notify = false (back to walking). Reset LW.fed at level load and in a LEVEL_DROPS entry. decorTick uses cdo('/Script/UMG.Image') (finding 0). hangarAmmoTick: look for each fed window's child 'WBP_Menu_IngameHangar_WeaponDetail_002' with childWidget first, and keep its FindAllOf (already rate-limited) only when no window yields a panel. Leave slotTexts' TextBlock walk as is until a WidgetTree descent is tested in game.
verify.est_saving: Removes a 35-71 ms walk (2-4 frames) every 0.5 s while on the ground at the airfield (~17-35 ms a tick averaged there), plus ~3 ms per decor pass from the UMG.Image lookup

kept.title: levelGoing() probes with SV_UnitAlive twice a tick (0.75 ms each); SV_UnitAlive's VirtualQuery-per-unit cost also hits rounds once a second per flight
kept.where: sv_core.lua:268-279 levelGoing(): pcall(SV_UnitAlive, CFG.pool[1]) every 0.1 s. In practice that is every half: leaveNow at sv_main.lua:509-511 and :601-603, plus walkHold() before any FindAllOf. runtime/survival_rt.c:1514-1523 UnitAlive: FindDesc (:1337, a UnitDescList scan plus a U.valuePtr name lookup), then RegisteredUnit (:1375-1383: Readable(), a VirtualQuery syscall, per phase-list unit, plus UnitId's vtable Readable), then UnitArrayNum (another U.valuePtr). The same native is called per flight up once a second by roundsTick (sv_rounds.lua:1346-1348, 1379-1381) and per due order by ordersTick (:1140)
kept.perf_part: leave check 1.1/3 (4%) solo, 0.6/2 Alicorn. natives: SV_UnitAlive 2.1 a tick, 1.59 ms (about 0.75 ms a call)
kept.frequency: Twice a tick (the probe). In late rounds, also once a second for each of 20-35 flights
kept.cost: 1.1-1.5 ms a tick for the probe alone. In late rounds the per-flight loop is about 20-35 x 0.75+ ms (15-30 ms) in one half once a second; this growth is not measured on 0.73.78, though the 0.73.70 late rounds show 'rounds' worst 130-305 ms
kept.fix: (a) The probe needs only SpawnerReady()'s code (-1/-6 against ready). Add a native SV_SpawnerOk() (12 characters, within hard rule 25) that returns SpawnerReady(), so RcDrain still runs on the same cadence. levelGoing calls it instead of SV_UnitAlive and falls back to SV_UnitAlive when it's missing (treat 1 as 'answered'). (b) In the native, cache FindDesc results by name (reset in SV_Reset). In RegisteredUnit, test units with uobj.h UObjLive() (GUObjectArray, no syscall) instead of Readable(), and keep the last unit pointer per desc id, checked against the list. Lua-only interim: probe in the first half only (0.25 s), halving the cost
kept.gameplay_note: (a) and (b) give identical answers. The interim adds at most 125 ms to the 1 s latch before kills stop paying on a quit; levelGate's SV_LevelGone teardown gate runs first in each half anyway
kept.risk: Low. Needs a runtime build: the hard rule 55 log-line fix is in, and the new name fits the 15-character limit

verify.cost_check: levelGoing (sv_core.lua:261-305): `local every = LEAVE.why and 1 or 0.1` ... `ok, r = pcall(SV_UnitAlive, u)` with u = CFG.pool[1]. It is called by leaveNow in both halves (sv_main.lua:509, :601) and by walkHold() before every FindAllOf. The halves are 125 ms apart, so the 0.1 s limit lets almost every half probe. Natives line: 'SV_UnitAlive 2.1 a tick 1.59 ms (worst 3)', which is the per-tick total, so ~0.75 ms a call (os.clock is 1 ms-quantised on Windows but the average is unbiased). 'leave check 1.1/3'. The native UnitAlive (survival_rt.c:1514-1523) runs SpawnerReady (FindSpawner, TeardownCheck, VCall world, RcDrain), then MakeName (FName ctor), FindDesc (U.valuePtr + name scan), then RegisteredUnit (:1375-1383: a VirtualQuery via `Readable(u, LY.idIface + 8)` and another in UnitId for every phase-list unit), then another U.valuePtr. Confirmed: roundsTick calls SV_UnitAlive per flight in D.up once a second (sv_rounds.lua:1346-1348, 1379-1381), and ordersTick per due order (:1140). Not shown: the claimed 15-30 ms late-round cost. Per-call cost probably scales with the phase list size, but 0.73.70's 'rounds worst 130-305' also includes spawns (SV_Spawn worst 181 ms in the Alicorn minute), so that growth is unmeasured.
verify.gameplay_check: (a) gives the same answers (SpawnerReady's -1/-5/-6/1 map onto levelGoing's cases; a ready spawner counts as 'answered'). Interim (probe at most every 0.2 s): the 1 s soft latch lands at 1.0-1.25 s instead of 1.0-1.125 s after the spawner goes. levelGate's SV_LevelGone gate closes first anyway, so no kill paid or refused changes in practice. (b) is the same per-flight answer.
verify.safety_check: (a) needs a runtime build. 'SV_SpawnerOk' is 12 characters (hard rule 25), and the registration-line overflow is fixed (hard rule 55, 0.32.23). Keep TeardownCheck and RcDrain in it (SpawnerReady already has both). Lua falls back to SV_UnitAlive when the function is missing. (b) as proposed is NOT safe: uobj.h UObjLive dereferences `o + 0xC` with no Readable guard, so replacing Readable() with UObjLive for phase-list pointers trades a syscall for a possible access violation on unmapped memory. A desc-pointer cache must be keyed on g_wd and the UnitDescList data pointer and dropped in SV_Reset.

Per tick: the music hold (sv_main.lua 563, every tick); shopTick (sv_shop.lua 823, every tick in flight, because RUN.dirty stays set until you're back on the airfield); TAC fighting() (sv_tactical.lua 20-22, 269); decorTick, hangarAmmoTick and ammoTick (each every other tick: sv_shop.lua 72, sv_main.lua 75, sv_flights.lua 307). kept.fix: Memoize per game-thread callback. In sv_main.lua's loop (888-923), set FRAME = (FRAME or 0) + 1 at the start of each ExecuteInGameThread callback and FRAME = nil at its end. playerLocation() then keeps { frame, value } and returns a copy of the value read for the current FRAME (nil cached too). Outside a tick (key binds, NotifyOnNewObject callbacks) FRAME is nil, so they always read fresh. Clear the memo after our own code moves or replaces the plane inside a half (sv_down.lua's SV_Respawn and loiter calls, co-op rejoin).
kept.gameplay_note: The world doesn't advance during one game-thread callback, so each caller gets exactly what it reads today.
kept.risk: A teleport by our own code within a half must clear the memo. Return copies so no caller can edit the shared table. Low.

kept.title: Every mirrored object's health is polled with IsValid + HealthInternal 4 times a second: host hostTick over M.byId, joiner clientTick over M.copies

A Spaceport round (27 ships, 68 turrets, LCACs, 30 island units) costs about 12-15 ms.

SV_HpWatch(id, addr|0) registers or removes an object; call it from hostPlane, hostGround, bindCopy and bindGround, and when an id goes. SV_HpScan() returns 'id:h,...' only for entries whose HealthInternal changed since the last scan, and 'id:0' when the ref is gone. Clear the table in SV_CoopReset and when the teardown gate closes. hostTick then takes deaths and e.curHp from the scan only, and builds the 1-second 'hp' batch from entries whose curHp ~= sentHp. clientTick runs its per-copy logic only for scanned ids, plus a Lua set of copies sitting at the floor (the h <= FLOOR_IN branch that reads the damage map). Native table: use CoRefSet/CoRefGet, which check vtable, index and name, so they also catch a reused address. Clear it in SV_CoopReset, on g_teardown and on COOP.levelDrop. Fall back to the Lua loop when g_offHealth < 0 (CoHealth returns 1). Confirm HealthInternal is at one offset for both planes and non-plane LiveAIGameObjects (assert it the first time U.valuePtr runs on a ground object), or resolve the offset per class. Read health with a predeclared `local function hpOf(o) return o.HealthInternal end` and `pcall(hpOf, o)`, so there are no per-call closures. This drops one UE4SS call and two closures per object. Step 2 (native, medium). Add SV_HpWatch(id, addr|0) and SV_HpScan() -> 'id:h,...' for entries whose int32 HealthInternal changed, and 'id:0' for gone refs, in a table of ~1024 CoRef slots. The host takes deaths and curHp from the scan only. The joiner runs its per-copy block for scanned ids, for ids marked dirty wherever c.exp is set outside clientTick (copyScaled, the 'hp' handler, bind), and for a floor set (copies with 0 < h <= FLOOR_IN).

kept.cost: Measured at 0.75 ms per SV_UnitAlive with only 1-3 units on the phase list ('units (round 1 clear): 3'), so the list scan isn't the cost. SV_Ammo has SpawnerReady but no name lookups and comes out at about 0.3 ms (1.7 ms / 5.3 calls). That suggests roughly half of SV_UnitAlive is the name lookups and half the syscalls. kept.fix: In survival_rt.c: (a) Cache desc pointers by FName (index, number), reset when g_wd changes or at SV_Reset; a level's UnitDescList doesn't change. Also key the cache by the incoming wide string so MakeName runs once per name. (b) Find the offsets of UnitDescList and AliveChildAIGameObjects once (ptr - obj from the first U.valuePtr) and add them directly afterwards. (c) Replace Readable/LiveObject on UObjects with uobj.h:14 UObjLive / UObjAllocated (GUObjectArray reads, no syscall; g_uoChunks is already found), and the vtable Readable in VCall and UnitId with InGame (:240) / an image-range check. Lua side: a native SV_AmmoAll() that returns the 5 counts and 5 maxima from one PlayerWeapons call; ammoTick reads it once per 0.5 s into a table that the rest of ammoTick and UP.apply use instead of separate SV_Ammo calls.

UnitAlive (:1514-1523) calls SpawnerReady (:1311-1335), which runs TeardownCheck -> ObjGoneWhy (Readable) -> FindSpawner (LiveObject on g_spawner and PhaseWorldData: Readable(phase), LiveObject(wd)) -> VCall (2 Readable) -> LiveObject(world): about 7 VirtualQuery. Then MakeName (U.fname), FindDesc (U.valuePtr(g_wd, L"UnitDescList") by name plus a linear desc scan), RegisteredUnit (:1375-1384: Readable(u) plus Readable(vt) in UnitId for EACH unit scanned until it matches), and UnitArrayNum (valuePtr by name plus Readable). Important and not in the finding: RegisteredUnit's 2 VirtualQuery per unit scanned grow with the phase list (24-28 units by rounds 8-12 in the 2026-11-01 host logs), so a late-round call costs more than the measured 0.75 ms. VirtualQuery computes RegionSize by walking page-table entries, which is slow inside large committed heap regions. SV_Ammo: PlayerWeapons (:1625-1635) repeats SpawnerReady plus VCall and 5 Readable, then AmmoSlots 3 more; ammoTick calls SV_Ammo(k) for k = 0..4 every 0.5 s (sv_flights.lua:301-302).

Option (d) must key on the engine's frame counter or a per-callback stamp, NOT a 10-20 ms GetTickCount64 stamp: that has about 16 ms resolution and can span a frame boundary where the incremental purge frees the world, leaving the teardown gate unchecked on a freed spawner. Cache descs only while g_wd is unchanged, and clear the cache at SV_Reset and whenever FindSpawner resets g_wd. Cache FNames for positive results only (MakeName uses FNAME_Find). Cache the AliveChildAIGameObjects offset per unit class pointer (+0x10). Re-run uobj_test.sh, safecall_test.sh and the recycle test.

(c) In RegisteredUnit / UnitId / PhaseUnits / UnitArrayNum, use UObjAllocated(u) == 1 and InGame(vtable) instead of Readable. In SpawnerReady, check the world chain with UObjLive after one Readable of the kept pointer. kept.title: The native Log forces a disk flush on every line; SV_LogUnits writes the whole unit list at every round start and clear
kept.where: survival_rt.c:85-114 Log: WriteFile, then FlushFileBuffers(g_log) at :111 for every line, inside a spin lock (:90) that the worker-thread guards' logs share. LogUnits :1526-1544 writes one line per unit on the phase list (plus a FindDescById scan and 2 by-name lookups per unit). Spawn :1452-1469 and Recycle :1395-1419 write 1-2 lines per flight spawn. Lua calls SV_LogUnits every round at sv_rounds.lua:1068 (startRound) and :1414 (round clear).
kept.perf_part: rounds worst 130-305 (co-op hosts' round start and clear ticks, together with the walks above); SV_Spawn worst 18 ms for a normal flight
kept.frequency: Every native log line. Bursts of N+1 lines at each round start and clear; N was 24-28 units by rounds 10-12 in the 2026-11-01 host logs (s2_host 'units (round 12 start): 28 on the phase's list'). 1-2 lines per flight spawn.
kept.cost: Unmeasured. FlushFileBuffers makes the OS write the file's dirty data and flush the drive's cache: typically about 1-5 ms on an SSD and 10-30 ms on a hard disk. 29 flushed lines at a round start or clear is about 30-150 ms on an SSD and several hundred ms on an HDD, all on the game thread. A worker thread flushing while it holds g_logLock also stalls a game-thread Log spinning on Sleep(0).
kept.fix: Drop FlushFileBuffers from Log, or flush at most once a second. WriteFile alone reaches the OS cache, which survives a game crash; Crumb (:167-205), the crash record, already writes without a flush. In sv_rounds.lua, call SV_LogUnits only with [log] verbose (logVerbose()); otherwise log just the count (a count-only argument to LogUnits). Optional: Lua's log (sv_core.lua:46-50) also print()s every line into UE4SS's console window (the testers' UE4SS.log starts 'Console created') and UE4SS.log, on top of AC8SurvivalMode_lua.log; a [log] echo = false would remove those console writes.
kept.gameplay_note: Logging only.
kept.risk: A power loss or OS crash (not a game crash) could lose the last lines the OS hadn't written yet.

verify.cost_check: survival_rt.c:107-112 Log: 'WriteFile(g_log, ...); FlushFileBuffers(g_log);' on every line, inside the g_logLock spin (:90, 'while (__sync_lock_test_and_set(&g_logLock, 1)) Sleep(0);'). Crumb (:167-205) writes without a flush. Lua's log (sv_core.lua:46-50) is unbuffered but never fsyncs. LogUnits (:1526-1544) writes 1 + N lines, each with Readable, FindDescById's scan and 2 by-name UnitArrayNum. It is called at sv_rounds.lua:1068 (round start) and :1414 (round clear). The 2026-11-01 host logs: 'units (round 8 clear): 28 on the phase's list', so 29 flushed lines in one tick; about 40 native lines a minute at peak; 1,238 lines in s4's 80 minutes. Cost unmeasured, but FlushFileBuffers forces an NTFS metadata log write and a device cache flush: about 0.5-5 ms on SSDs, 10-30 ms on HDDs.
verify.gameplay_check: None; logging only.
verify.safety_check: Data written with WriteFile sits in the OS cache and survives a game crash. Only a power loss or OS crash loses unflushed lines, which is what the crash record (Crumb) already accepts. Removing the flush also shortens how long a worker thread (the target / effect guards' logs) holds g_logLock while the game thread spins on Sleep(0).

Gate the per-unit lines behind a flag Lua passes when [log] verbose (logVerbose()) is on, e.g. SV_LogUnits(why, 1): a small native argument change. The per-unit work (FindDescById, 2 by-name lookups and VirtualQuery per unit) is skipped too. The Lua print() echo to the console is a separate, optional change.
verify.est_saving: About 30-150 ms (SSD) or several hundred ms (HDD) of flushes per round start and clear, plus 1-5 ms per flight spawn's log lines. LogUnits' per-unit lookups save a few more ms per round edge. Unmeasured: check with a perf line around a round clear before and after.

kept.title: Native Log() writes every line through to the disk (FlushFileBuffers under a spin lock) on the game thread and on worker threads
kept.where: survival_rt.c Log() 85-114: spin lock with Sleep(0) at 90, FlushFileBuffers(g_log) at 111. Where the bursts come from: LogUnits 1526-1543 writes N+1 lines at every round start and clear (sv_rounds.lua:1068/1414); Spawn 1465 and Recycle 1413-1421 write 1-2 lines per SV_Spawn, and the refused-spawn line at 1401 can come up to 8 times a second; coop.c CoStep's minute stats at 1384-1413 write 2 lines plus one per player in a single frame; flight.c FlNetLog 671-684 writes a line per real plane in one frame, plus FnLog 1197 and FdLog 1367. Lines written from worker threads: the guards in flight.c TcCheck 1790-1823 and pathguard.h 62-79. Their per-call logging is already rate-limited (first 4, then powers of two), so that part is fine.
kept.perf_part: rounds worst 120-156 ms in every perf period of the 0.73.70 co-op host (one spike per round transition) and 19 ms solo; SV_Spawn worst 18 ms solo and 181 ms in the Alicorn round; co-op spikes once a minute that no perf part times
kept.frequency: 30-70 native lines a minute in co-op (s2/s4 host logs). The s4 host wrote 29 lines in one frame at round 11's clear (13:36:32) and again at round 12's start (13:37:03), with 28 units on the phase list. Co-op adds bursts of 5-10 lines in one frame every minute.
kept.cost: FlushFileBuffers makes the thread wait until the data, the NTFS metadata and the device's cache flush reach the disk. That is about 1-10 ms on an SSD and 10-30 ms or more on an HDD or a busy disk (the 0.73.70 host had 30 GB committed, so it was also paging). A 29-line LogUnits burst therefore costs about 30-300 ms on the game thread in one frame, and each SV_Spawn adds 1-3 ms or more. When a guard logs from a worker thread, the flush happens inside a ParallelFor the frame is waiting on, and every other thread that tries to log spins on Sleep(0) until it ends.
kept.fix: Delete FlushFileBuffers(g_log) at survival_rt.c:111. WriteFile already hands the bytes to the OS cache, and the OS cache outlives a game crash. The crumbs file (Crumb 167-206) already depends on exactly that and never flushes. Also: (a) LogUnits builds the whole list into one buffer and writes it in a single WriteFile; Lua can pass a flag to skip it unless [log] verbose. (b) The guards' worker-thread Log/Crumb calls go into a small lock-free ring that FlightInputHook drains on the game thread, so a ParallelFor never waits on file I/O. (c) The Sleep(0) spin locks at 90 and 172 can become an SRWLOCK.
kept.gameplay_note: The log content is unchanged; only the moment the bytes reach the disk changes.
kept.risk: Only an OS crash or power loss could lose the last few seconds of AC8SurvivalMode.log; a game crash cannot, because the data is already in the OS cache. The crumbs file stays as it is for crash forensics.

verify.cost_check: survival_rt.c Log() 85-114: every line does `WriteFile(g_log, ...); FlushFileBuffers(g_log);` (110-111) under `while (__sync_lock_test_and_set(&g_logLock, 1)) Sleep(0);` (90). Crumb (167-206) does WriteFile only, with its comment saying the system keeps what was written if the game crashes, so the author already relies on the OS cache. Bursts are real. LogUnits (1526-1543) writes 1+N lines from sv_rounds.lua:1068 (round start) and :1414 (round clear), both inside the timed 'rounds' part. s4 host log: 29 lines at 13:36:32 (round 11 clear) and 29 at 13:37:03 (round 12 start), with 28 units on the phase list. Spawn writes 1465; Recycle writes 1409/1413-1418 and RcDrain one more per deferred destroy. Rates are lower than claimed on average: s1/s2/s3/s4 hosts wrote 12-18 native lines a minute, with peaks of 59-70 a minute and 29-46 lines in one second. The 0.73.70 hosts' 'rounds' worst was 107-309 ms in every perf period (rounds 0.9/120, 1.8/146 ... 3.5/305, 5.5/309), which fits about 30-45 flushed lines at each round transition. Worker-thread logs (TcCheck, pathguard OnPathTrackItem) are rate-limited (n<=4 or a power of two), so they are rare, but each of those flushes inside the ParallelFor.
verify.gameplay_check: None. The log text and its order are the same; only when the bytes reach the disk changes. No round, timing or HUD effect.
verify.safety_check: WriteFile to a normal cached handle puts the data in the system cache, which survives a game crash, a hang or a kill. Only a BSOD or power loss could lose the last seconds, the same exposure the crumbs file already accepts. No object reads, no threading change (the spin lock is held for about 10-20 µs instead of milliseconds, so worker threads that log rarely spin). No Lua rules are involved.
verify.refined_fix: Delete `FlushFileBuffers(g_log);` at survival_rt.c:111. That one line is the whole fix. Optional extras: an SRWLOCK in place of the Sleep(0) spin, and building LogUnits into one buffer for a single WriteFile. The lock-free worker ring in (b) isn't worth it: with the flush gone a rate-limited worker log costs one WriteFile of about 5-20 µs. Keep LogUnits as it is (it is the spawn-diagnosis record); it is cheap without the flush.
verify.est_saving: About 1-10 ms per native line on an SSD (10-30+ ms on an HDD or busy disk). This removes a 30-300 ms hitch at every round start and clear (the 120-310 ms 'rounds' worst seen on the co-op hosts) and 1-10 ms from each SV_Spawn or recycle line.

kept.title: SV_UnitAlive, Spawn, Recycle and LogUnits repeat a name lookup, two UE4SS property lookups and 2 VirtualQuery calls per listed unit on every call
kept.where: UnitAlive 1514-1523 calls: MakeName 1027-1034 (UE4SS FName constructor); FindDesc 1337-1346 (U.valuePtr(g_wd, L"UnitDescList"), then a linear scan of the 0xB0-byte descs); RegisteredUnit 1375-1384 (PhaseUnits 1359-1365 does 2 Readable, then each listed unit gets Readable(u), UnitId 1367-1373's Readable of the vtable slot, and a virtual call); UnitArrayNum 1386-1391 (U.valuePtr(unit, L"AliveChildAIGameObjects") plus a Readable). The same pattern is in Spawn 1452-1470, Recycle 1395-1423, SetAircraft, SetLevel, LogUnits 1526-1543 (two UnitArrayNum, NameText and FindDescById per unit) and L_Recycle. Readable (218-224) is a VirtualQuery syscall.
kept.perf_part: Perf lines: SV_UnitAlive 2.1 calls a tick for 1.59 ms (0.76 ms a call, solo round 1, 1-3 units listed) and 1.3 a tick for 0.97 ms (Alicorn round). 'leave check' 1.1 ms a tick is one SV_UnitAlive per half (sv_core.lua:278). 0.73.70 co-op host: 'rounds' grew from 0.1 to 8.3 ms a tick and 'allies' from 0.6 to 3.8 ms a tick over rounds 1-12, while the phase list grew to 28 units.
kept.frequency: Every Lua call: the leave check every half (8 a second); the round probe once a second for every flight in D.up (sv_rounds.lua:1346-1349 and 1378-1382); ALLY.alive's share each tick; the clean-up checks; the specials' loops (sv_alicorn deck, sv_amphib, sv_ladon, sv_director).
kept.cost: VirtualQuery is a syscall, and to compute RegionSize it walks the page tables of the whole committed run. UE5's binned allocator commits objects in very large runs, so each call costs tens of µs on a big heap. The perf lines imply about 20-45 µs on Saint Alessia's machine (12.7 GB). One call is about 12-16 VirtualQuery with 1-3 units listed (0.5-0.75 ms) and grows by 2 per listed unit. With 28 units and 15-20 flights up, the once-a-second probe is about 600-760 VirtualQuery, or 15-33 ms in one tick. That averages out to the 8.3 ms a tick that 'rounds' measured.
kept.fix: (a) Cache the reflected offsets once, as CoResolve (coop.c:426-445) already does for RootComponent: UnitDescList on the world-data class, and AliveChildAIGameObjects / ChildAIGameObjects per unit UClass (a 4-8 entry {class, offset} table). (b) Add a small hash from the wide unit name Lua passes to {FNameRaw, desc index}. Validate each hit against the UnitDescList data pointer and count and the desc's own FName, and rebuild on any change. This removes MakeName and the scan. (c) In RegisteredUnit, test each listed unit with UObjLive (GUObjectArray only, about 20 ns) and its vtable with InGame() (vtables are in the exe image) instead of two VirtualQuery calls. PhaseUnits' array lives inside the live spawner (its GlobalPhase), so it needs only the existing num/max sanity bounds. Optionally keep an id-to-unit table rebuilt only when the list's data or count changes. Expected cost: about 1-3 µs a call.
kept.gameplay_note: The answers are the same. Every cache is validated against the live arrays and GUObjectArray and rebuilt when they change.
kept.risk: A stale cache would give a wrong alive count, so a round could end early or late. Contain it by validating every hit (desc FName equal, array data/count unchanged, unit live in GUObjectArray), falling back to today's path when GUObjectArray isn't found, and logging any mismatch against the old path for one test session.

verify.cost_check: UnitAlive 1514-1523: SpawnerReady() (7 VirtualQuery: ObjGoneWhy's Readable in TeardownCheck; FindSpawner's fast path LiveObject(g_spawner), PhaseWorldData's Readable + LiveObject(wd); VCall's 2 Readables; LiveObject(world)), then MakeName (U.fname), FindDesc (`U.valuePtr(g_wd, L"UnitDescList")` + scan), RegisteredUnit (PhaseUnits: `Readable(a, sizeof(*a))` + `Readable(a->data, num*8)`; per listed unit until the match: `Readable(u, LY.idIface + 8)` + UnitId's `Readable(vt + LY.idSlot / 8, 8)`) and UnitArrayNum (`U.valuePtr(unit, L"AliveChildAIGameObjects")` + Readable). That is 10 + 2k VirtualQuery for k units scanned. Callers verified: levelGoing() calls SV_UnitAlive(CFG.pool[1]) at most every 0.1 s, once per half (sv_core.lua 270-279, called through leaveNow in both halves: sv_main 509, 601). sv_rounds.lua 1346-1349 ('wave') and 1378-1382 ('fighting') call SV_UnitAlive for every flight in D.up once a second. The phase list keeps dead flights (s4: 28 units, most `0 of N alive`), so k grows over the run. Measured: 'SV_UnitAlive 2.1 a tick 1.59 ms' (0.76 ms a call) solo and 1.3 a tick 0.97 ms in the Alicorn round. 'leave check' 1.1 ms a tick is about 2 calls. The per-VirtualQuery cost of ~20-50 µs is inferred, but it agrees with SV_Ammo's ~0.26 ms a call, which does almost nothing besides about 17 VirtualQuery. That process had 30 GB committed.
verify.gameplay_check: None, as long as the answers are identical. A wrong answer would matter a lot: sv_rounds drops a flight from D.up on any answer <= 0 (`else D.up[u] = nil`), which can end a round or a wave early, and a -1/-6 latches levelGoing (no kills paid). So the fix must never produce a false 'not ready' or 0.
verify.safety_check: (c) as proposed (UObjLive on each listed unit) reads u+0xC and also refuses GC-unreachable objects. That adds nothing the game's own IsUnitIdSpawned doesn't already rely on (it calls the same vfunc on every listed unit with no checks), and it brings a false-negative risk. Better: drop the per-unit Readable, keep `InGame(vt + slot)` for the vtable (vtables live in the exe image), and rely on SpawnerReady's teardown gate for the list being freed. g_phase is inside the live spawner (U.valuePtr(spawner, "GlobalPhase")), so the TArray header needs only the num/max bounds. The id-to-unit table in (b)/'optionally' is unsafe as described: Spawn's Recycle + spawn removes one unit and appends one in the same call, so data and count can be unchanged while the contents changed. Skip it; a Readable-free linear scan of 28 units costs well under a microsecond. FName cache: FNames never change once created, so a hit-only {wide name -> FNameRaw} cache is permanently valid; never cache misses (world data can load later). Cache offsets per UClass (*(obj+0x10)), as CoResolve does. Teardown: keep SpawnerReady first. No Lua change.
verify.refined_fix: In survival_rt.c: (1) offsets cached per class: UnitDescList on g_wd's class, AliveChildAIGameObjects / ChildAIGameObjects in a 4-8 entry {UClass*, offset} table, with today's U.valuePtr as the miss path; (2) MakeName through a small hit-only cache; (3) RegisteredUnit / PhaseUnits / LogUnits: no per-unit Readable, `InGame(vt + LY.idSlot/8)` before the vfunc call, the num/max bounds kept, a linear scan kept (no id map); (4) UnitArrayNum reads the TArray header inside the live unit with no Readable, using the cached offset. The SpawnerReady part is finding 2's fix; do both together. Log one comparison against the old path per unit name for the first test session.
verify.est_saving: From about 10+2k VirtualQuery a call (~0.75 ms measured solo, more with a long phase list) to about 2-5 µs. Leave check ~1 ms a tick down to ~0.02; the once-a-second round probe in late co-op rounds (15-20 flights, 28 listed units) goes from about 15-35 ms in one tick to under 0.2 ms, which removes most of the 0.1 -> 8.3 ms a tick growth in 'rounds' and part of 'allies'.

kept.perf_part: SV_ObjChain runs 25-29 times a tick (perf 'natives' line). It is counted but not timed, because sv_main.lua:748 assumes it costs no more than a clock read. kept.fix: Check memory only for the first object: that is the address Lua passed, and the case hotfix8 fixed (released memory). Walk the outers with UObjLive alone. An object being purged carries the unreachable flag that UObjLive already refuses, so the walk stops before reading that object's outer. The first check can also become a zero-cost probe instead of a VirtualQuery: one fixed load instruction whose access violation the existing VEH (safecall.h ScVeh) skips to a fallback label.

If the first object passes Readable + UObjLive (its slot holds it, it isn't garbage or unreachable), its OuterPrivate is kept reachable by the GC (the outer is always a strong reference and is never eliminated), so the outer is allocated and reading outer+0xC/+0x20 is safe. An unreachable inner is refused before its outer is read, and objects are freed only after being flagged unreachable (incremental or async purge). The VEH probe for the first object (ScCall4 around a 2-load function) is a possible later step, at about 50 ns instead of one VirtualQuery, but it depends on our handler being first in the VEH chain. Optional.

kept.where: Lua: sv_flights.lua roundClock 393-406 calls sv_spawn.lua gameClock 6-11 and gamePaused 13-17. Each does cdo() (StaticFindObject + valid) and then a UE4SS reflected UFunction call (GameplayStatics.GetTimeSeconds / IsGamePaused). This is timed as 'clock' at sv_main.lua 544-547. Runtime: a new L_GameClock next to L_UnitAlive (survival_rt.c:2642), registered with the other functions at 3325-3343.

kept.frequency: Every first half (4 times a second)
kept.cost: 6.3 ms a tick on Saint Alessia's machine for 2 StaticFindObject, 2 IsValid and 2 reflected UFunction calls through UE4SS.
kept.fix: Add SV_GameClock(), returning 'seconds,paused' for the spawner's world that SpawnerReady keeps. Resolve once the two native functions behind UGameplayStatics::GetTimeSeconds and ::IsGamePaused: U.findObject on '/Script/Engine.GameplayStatics:GetTimeSeconds' (and IsGamePaused), then follow their Func thunks to the call targets, checked by code shape like the runtime's other resolutions. Call them with g_spawner as the world context. Lua uses SV_GameClock when it exists and gameClock otherwise. For the first ~20 ticks, compare it with GetTimeSeconds and keep Lua's path if they disagree. The Lua-side first step (caching the two CDOs instead of calling StaticFindObject every time) may already recover much of the cost.
kept.gameplay_note: Same values from the same engine functions, called natively.
kept.risk: Finding the thunks' targets may break after a game patch. This is contained by the code-shape check, the agreement check and the Lua fallback.

verify.cost_check: The 'clock' part (sv_main.lua 544-547) times roundClock(tick) + pcall(SND.setPaused, paused). SND.setPaused returns at once unless the pause state changes (sv_sound.lua 187-192). roundClock (sv_flights.lua 393-406) calls gameClock: cdo() = StaticFindObject + valid (sv_ai.lua 1062), valid(pc), gs:GetTimeSeconds(pc). It calls gamePaused (cdo again + gs:IsGamePaused(pc)) whenever t ~= D.now, which is every unpaused pass. That is 2 StaticFindObject, 3 IsValid and 2 reflected UFunction calls once a tick, and the measured 6.3 ms (solo) / 6.8 ms (Alicorn) a tick is real. What the finding can't support is which of these calls costs the time: each should be microseconds on a normal machine, so most of the 6 ms is unexplained UE4SS overhead on that PC (the same machine shows 61-71 ms FindAllOf walks and 0.26 ms SV_Ammo calls). Following the thunks by 'code shape' is the most fragile route offered.
verify.gameplay_check: None if the values are identical. Pitfall: if SV_GameClock returns 'not ready' early in a level (SpawnerReady needs the spawner) and roundClock treats that as nil, then after 20 ticks D.clock becomes 'ticks' (real time: rounds keep running while paused), a real gameplay change. The native path must fall back to the Lua path on any error, never return nil. Skipping gamePaused when the clock advanced would delay the pause by one pass (250 ms) for Survival's sounds, HUD and music. Don't do that.
verify.safety_check: Lua step: Default__GameplayStatics is the CDO of a native /Script class; it is rooted and never freed, so caching it once per session is safe (re-check it with valid() or liveObj(), which are cheap on a permanent object). It removes both StaticFindObject calls and two userdata creations. pc is still checked with valid() each call. Native step: use g_spawner (and the world SpawnerReady already keeps) only after SpawnerReady() == 1. Prefer calling the cached UFunction through ProcessEvent on the cached CDO (UFunctions and CDOs of native classes are permanent) over parsing exec thunks. If thunks are parsed, keep the code-shape check, the 20-tick agreement check and the Lua fallback. Teardown: SpawnerReady already gates. kept.title: ScCall4 does a full CONTEXT capture plus three TLS API calls per guarded call (the VEH itself is installed only once)
kept.where: safecall.h: ScInit 40-55 calls AddVectoredExceptionHandler once, from TgtInstall at startup; that part is fine. ScCall4 58-81 calls TlsGetValue, RtlCaptureContext into a 1232-byte frame, and TlsSetValue twice on every call. ScVeh 26-37 copies the 1232 bytes back after a fault. Callers: pathguard.h OnPathTrackItem 52-81 (every path tracker, every frame) and flight.c TcCheck 1808-1813 (the 17 TCK_CATCH event classes).
kept.perf_part: Unmeasured. The 5-minute 'guard: ... the last 5 minutes: about N calls (N a second)' lines from TgtLog and PtLog report the call rates, but none of the sample logs contain them.
kept.frequency: Every AI path tracker, every frame, on the ParallelFor workers (one per unit and per AI object: a few hundred in the Alicorn round with its 131 parked pools), and every guarded event Match.
kept.cost: About 50-100 ns a call: the context capture is 60-100 instructions, plus the TLS calls and a 1.2 KB stack frame. With a few hundred trackers that is about 20-60 µs of worker time a frame, and the frame waits for the ParallelFor.
kept.fix: Keep the single handler. Replace RtlCaptureContext with a minimal capture: clang's __builtin_setjmp saves only the frame pointer, resume address and stack pointer, and the compiler spills every callee-saved register around it. In ScVeh, set the CONTEXT's Rip, Rsp and Rbp from that buffer. Keep the frame pointer in a _Thread_local variable instead of calling TlsGetValue/TlsSetValue. tools/checks/safecall_test.c and pathguard_test.c already exercise a made-up fault and can prove the new path.
kept.gameplay_note: The same faults are caught with the same answers.
kept.risk: A wrong resume state would crash on the first caught fault. This is contained by safecall_test/pathguard_test and by keeping the RtlCaptureContext path behind a switch.

verify.cost_check: safecall.h ScCall4 58-81 really does `g_scTlsGet(g_scTls)`, `g_scCapture(fr.ctx)` (RtlCaptureContext into a 0x4D0-byte frame) and `g_scTlsSet` twice on every call. ScInit adds the VEH once. Callers: pathguard.h OnPathTrackItem calls ScCall4(PtGuarded, ...) for every path tracker every frame on ParallelFor workers, and TcCheck calls it only for TCK_CATCH classes (17 of 37 per the logs). Cost: about 40-100 ns a call (TlsGetValue and TlsSetValue are a few ns each, RtlCaptureContext is about 40 stores). Even 500 trackers is about 20-50 µs of worker CPU a frame, spread over the workers: a few µs of frame time. That is negligible next to the trackers' own spline work and to the VirtualQuery costs in findings 1-6. No sample log has the 5-minute 'guard: ... calls' line to measure it.
verify.gameplay_check: None in principle (same faults caught, same answers).
verify.safety_check: The proposed fix carries real risk for almost no gain. (1) `_Thread_local` needs the PE TLS directory (_tls_used / _tls_index), which the CRT's tlssup normally provides; the runtime is built freestanding with `lld-link /nodefaultlib` (runtime/build.sh 40-50), so it would not link without a hand-written TLS directory. (2) Resuming from the VEH by setting Rip/Rsp/Rbp from a __builtin_setjmp buffer depends on LLVM's internal SjLj layout and on every callee-saved register (XMM6-15 on Win64) being treated as clobbered. A wrong state crashes on the first caught fault, which is exactly the rare path the guard exists for and that tests rarely exercise in game.
verify.refined_fix: Don't change it. If anything, read the TLS slot straight from the TEB (gs:[0x1480 + 8*slot] for slots < 64) instead of TlsGetValue/TlsSetValue, which keeps RtlCaptureContext and the proven resume path and saves about 10 ns a call. First add the sampled call rate (already in PtLog/TgtLog) to the logs that get collected.
verify.est_saving: At most a few µs of frame time (about 20-50 µs of worker CPU a frame at a few hundred trackers). Not measurable against a 16.7 ms frame.

kept.fix: Remove FlushFileBuffers(g_log) at survival_rt.c:111 and keep the plain WriteFile. If a durable copy is still wanted, flush once at DLL detach or when the teardown gate closes, never per line. Rebuild and bump the runtime; nothing else changes.
kept.gameplay_note: Log output is the same; only the disk sync goes.
kept.risk: Very low. After a game crash the log and crumbs stay complete, since WriteFile data is already with the OS. crumbs.log is unaffected: Crumb() never flushed and stays written at once.

verify.cost_check: The finding holds. survival_rt.c Log(): the spin lock `while (__sync_lock_test_and_set(&g_logLock, 1)) Sleep(0);`, then `WriteFile(g_log, utf8, (DWORD)n, &put, NULL); FlushFileBuffers(g_log);` (line 111) for every line. The handle is opened with plain FILE_ATTRIBUTE_NORMAL (line 137), so the per-line disk sync comes only from that call. Crumb() (lines 167-205) uses WriteFile alone. Game-thread callers confirmed: LogUnits (1526-1544) writes 1 + one line per unit and runs from sv_rounds.lua:1068/1414 inside roundsTick; Spawn writes `spawn %s: up` (line 1466) and Recycle adds its own line; SndLoad logs once per file. In solo, only SV_LogUnits runs between them; in co-op a 'cr' send is also there. s4 host: r1 9.1 ms (4 lines), r6 31 ms (18), r8 50.5 ms (23), r10 50.3 ms (28), r11 59.9 ms (29). 0.73.78 Alicorn solo r1: 9.5 ms (4). verify.gameplay_check: Nothing a player can see. The log text stays the same; only the forced disk sync per line goes. It does remove 50-110 ms stalls at round starts and clears, plus about 4 ms per flight spawned, which players currently feel as hitches.
verify.safety_check: Crash safety is unchanged. Data handed to WriteFile sits in the OS cache and reaches disk after a game crash, a hang killed from Task Manager, or a normal exit, which is the same guarantee Crumb() relies on. Only a BSOD or power loss could drop the last lines. Without the flush the lock is held for less time, so contention with worker-thread guard lines drops. There is no Lua, co-op protocol or teardown impact. It is a runtime change, so it needs a version bump, a new build hash (register the zip on /admin), and every co-op player on the same build (CoSameVer).

kept.title: VALKA's song and railgun sounds load synchronously on first play, during the fight (a 45.6 MB WAV read on the game thread)
kept.where: sv_sound.lua SND.id 53-66 calls SV_SndLoad(file) lazily on first play. SND.songStart 135-137 is called at her mood start (sv_anomalies.lua:1696) and on co-op joiners at "vm|1" (sv_coop.lua:97). Her railgun sound events are at sv_anomalies.lua:991-1020. The native SndLoad (survival_rt.c ~2375-2425) does CreateFileW, then one ReadFile of the whole file (up to 64 MB) into a malloc'd buffer, a parse, and a Log line with a flush.
kept.perf_part: Unmeasured by the perf line; measured from UE4SS.log timestamps in the VALKA test of 2026-11-03
kept.frequency: Once per VALKA round (each file once a session; SND.ids keeps them). It lands at her reveal and on her first shots, in combat, on every game in co-op.
kept.cost: 106 ms between 'sound: master -24 dB' (13:22:23.690, logged inside SND.id just before SV_SndLoad) and 'sound: the song valka/Void.wav playing' (23.796). Void.wav is 11,389,376 stereo 16-bit frames, 45.6 MB. Then charge_start and charge_loop (0.8 + 5.5 MB) at the opener charge (13:22:28). Six more files (charge_end, shot_main, whoosh_2, shot_eml_1-3, shot_far; about 5 MB) load at her opener shot: 98 ms between the Lua lines around it at 13:22:35, likely mostly these loads. whoosh_1/3/4 load later in the fight (13:22:37, 13:22:57, 13:23:16).
kept.fix: Preload every file of the song (c.song.file) and of CFG.sound.valka.* with SND.id(file), one file per tick. Do it in the break when the NEXT row says VALKA (on a joiner, when the host's "rnd" special field says valka), or at the latest at the round's start, before her arrive_s. The ids stay in SND.ids exactly as after a first play. Longer term: let SV_SndLoad read on a worker thread and hand back the id when ready.
kept.gameplay_note: Same sounds at the same moments; only the load time moves.
kept.risk: Low. About 57 MB becomes resident a little earlier (it stays loaded after first play anyway). A load in the break still hitches, but out of combat, and less if spread one file per tick.

verify.cost_check: sv_sound.lua SND.id (53-66) calls `SV_SndMaster` on the first use (the native log's 'XAudio2 2.9 up' is in the same second) and then `local id = SV_SndLoad(file)` lazily. SND.songStart (135-137) calls `SND.id(sc.file)` from SPC.V.mood (sv_anomalies.lua:1696, once the round's flying decoys are down) and on joiners at 'vm|1' (sv_coop.lua:97). Native SndLoad (survival_rt.c 2363-2425) does CreateFileW, `malloc((size_t)size)`, one `ReadFile(f, buf, (DWORD)size, ...)` of the whole file, the RIFF parse, and a Log with a flush, all on the game thread. VALKA log: 13:22:23.690 'sound: master -24 dB' to 13:22:23.796 'the song valka/Void.wav playing' = 106 ms. Native log: Void.wav 11,389,376 frames x 2 ch x 2 B = 45.6 MB. charge_start/charge_loop load at 13:22:28, and seven files at 13:22:35 between 'VALKA's round ... (class default)' (35.216) and 'opener shot from 15.8 km' (35.314) = 98 ms. whoosh_1/3/4 load later in the fight. CFG.sound.valka layers include `pick` lists (whoosh_1-4), 14 files in all.
verify.gameplay_check: None. The same sounds play at the same moments; only the file reads and the XAudio2 start move earlier, to a non-combat moment. Co-op joiners hear the song at the same 'vm|1' as now.
verify.safety_check: SND.ids caches each id for the session (false on failure, never retried), exactly as after a first play. 14 of the 64 SND_MAX_SOUNDS slots are used. About 57 MB becomes resident earlier; it stays resident after the first play anyway. No game objects are involved, so there is no liveAddr or teardown concern. Guard with CFG.sound.enabled, c.song.enabled ~= false and type(SV_SndLoad) == 'function'. In builds without VALKA or the song, the missing file is logged once, as today. The native read is still synchronous, so do it in the break or at round start, never mid-fight.
verify.refined_fix: Add SND.preload(list), which calls SND.id(file) for one file per tick from a queue built from CFG.specials.valka.song.file plus every `file` and every `pick[i][1]` of CFG.sound.valka.* (charge, charge_loop, charge_end, shot, pass). Start the queue in the break when the next round's special is VALKA (host: specialFor(D.round + 1) / the NEXT row; joiner: the host's 'rnd' special field), and at the latest when a round starts with D.special.kind == 'valka'. Her mood only starts once the decoys are down, tens of seconds later. The first SND.id also starts XAudio2 (SV_SndMaster), which moves out of combat too. Later, a native follow-up: SV_SndLoad reading on a worker thread and returning a pending id.
verify.est_saving: Removes a ~106 ms stall at VALKA's mood start, ~98 ms at her opener shot and a few smaller ones (whoosh_1/3/4) later in the fight, once per VALKA round per game (each co-op player too). These move to a break or round start, spread one file per tick: about 100 ms for Void.wav once and a few ms for each other file.

kept.title: (Outside the logging area, but over 0.5 ms a tick) The level-leaving probe calls SV_UnitAlive (~0.75 ms native) in both tick halves
kept.where: sv_core.lua levelGoing 262-308: `local every = LEAVE.why and 1 or 0.1` (line 273), then pcall(SV_UnitAlive, CFG.pool[1]) (line 278). It is called by leaveNow() in both halves (sv_main.lua:386, 510-511 and 602-603) and by walkHold() before every FindAllOf / FindFirstOf / walkBusy / svFlags stale check. The halves are 125 ms apart, so the 0.1 s limit lets it run in every half.
kept.perf_part: 'leave check 1.1/3' (4%, round 1 solo) and '0.6/2' (Alicorn). Natives line: 'SV_UnitAlive 2.1 a tick 1.59 ms' and '1.3 a tick 0.97 ms', about 0.75 ms per call; almost all of these calls come from this probe.
kept.frequency: About 2 calls a tick (8 a second) whenever a level has planes
kept.cost: About 1.1-1.5 ms a tick. It grows over a run, because the native call walks the spawner's whole unit list with memory checks.
kept.fix: Probe every 0.5 s (or 1 s): `local every = LEAVE.why and 1 or 0.5`. Since runtime 0.32.22 the teardown gate (levelGate() -> SV_LevelGone, first thing in each half) closes as soon as the spawner's world is freed or goes garbage, and the soft sign only latches after the spawner has been gone 1 s (LEAVE.badAt), so a 0.5 s probe adds at most 0.4 s to a backstop path. This saves about 0.75-1.1 ms a tick. Optional native follow-up for the runtime agent: cache UnitAlive's desc pointer per name and the AliveChildAIGameObjects offset instead of GetValuePtrByPropertyNameInChain on every call.
kept.gameplay_note: Same detection; the soft backstop may latch up to 0.4 s later. Real quits are caught by the teardown gate and the hard sign (svLevelOn false) as now.
kept.risk: Low-medium: the probe exists so quits don't pay kills. Vanished planes are held VANISH_HOLD_S (1 s) and the gate closes first, so the window stays covered. Check a Quit Mission with the 'level: Survival's level is going away' line.

verify.cost_check: sv_core.lua levelGoing: `local every = LEAVE.why and 1 or 0.1` (line 273), then `if u then ok, r = pcall(SV_UnitAlive, u) end` (line 278) when `now - LEAVE.probeAt >= every`. leaveNow() calls levelGoing() at the top of both halves (sv_main.lua 509-511 in probeTick, 600-603 in probeTickB), and the halves are 125 ms apart, so the 0.1 s limit lets it probe in each half. That is about 2 a tick, matching 'SV_UnitAlive 2.1 a tick 1.59 ms' (0.75 ms per call; sv_main wraps the global, so the probe's pcall(SV_UnitAlive) is counted) and 'leave check 1.1/3'. walkHold, vanishedTick and planeSweep reuse the cached LEAVE state within 0.1 s. Natively, each call runs SpawnerReady (VCall, LiveObject, RcDrain), MakeName, FindDesc (valuePtr plus a desc scan) and RegisteredUnit (a VirtualQuery plus a virtual UnitId call per listed unit), so the cost grows with the phase list.
verify.gameplay_check: None in practice. The soft 'spawner gone' sign may be seen up to about 0.4 s later and latch up to ~0.4 s later. Both 0.73.78 quits (Alicorn 13:52:09) show the runtime's teardown gate closing first ('teardown gate: closed ... it was freed', then Lua 'level gate: closed'); the soft sign never latched. VANISH_HOLD_S is 1.0 s while the soft sign already needs at least 1 s of bad answers, so the gate and svLevelOn already protect vanished-plane pays, not this probe. A short false 'spawner gone' at a pause-menu restart is less likely to be seen at all, which is benign.
verify.safety_check: No objects are kept. levelGate() (SV_LevelGone) still runs first in every half, and svLevelOn (the hard sign) is unchanged. walkHold also holds on svLevelOn, WALK.worldAt and SV_GcBusy (walkBusy), so walks during teardown are still held when the gate closes. Co-op joiners use the same code. Hard rules 23, 29 and 47 are untouched.
verify.refined_fix: Use `local every = LEAVE.why and 1 or 0.5` (0.25, i.e. once a tick, if a tighter backstop is wanted). Optional runtime follow-up: a cheap native (e.g. SV_SpawnerOk: SpawnerReady() only, no FName, desc or unit-list work) for this probe, so it costs microseconds at any rate. Check a Quit Mission still logs 'level gate: closed' / 'run over: left' and pays no kills.
verify.est_saving: About 0.7-1.1 ms a tick on average (6 of 8 native calls a second at ~0.75 ms each). More in late rounds as the phase list grows. It applies to every build, friends' zips included.

kept.title: Lua log() / crumb() are cheap as they are: no buffered Lua logger needed
kept.where: sv_core.lua:44-56: log() does print() to UE4SS, then LOG_FILE:write(os.date(...) .. s) on a handle with setvbuf("no"), one WriteFile per line and no flush. crumb() at :59 calls the native Crumb, which uses WriteFile only. CFG.log.verbose = false already keeps out the periodic ai:, flags and intensity lines.
kept.perf_part: Not a timed part; measured from UE4SS.log timestamps
kept.frequency: 20-130 lines a minute in play (co-op host peaks 102-126 a minute); about 300 in the startup minute at the main menu; in-game bursts of at most 24-33 lines in one tick (round starts with 'AI aircraft created' / 'maneuvers' lines)
kept.cost: About 30-40 µs a line: consecutive Survival lines are as little as 31-44 µs apart, and 13 'world:' lines took 0.4-0.5 ms. The worst in-game bursts (24-33 lines) took 2.4-8.8 ms including the work between lines, of which the log I/O is about 1-1.5 ms. That is under 0.05 ms a tick on average. The large per-line strings (perf, flags, weapons summaries) are logged once a minute or rarely. Strings are built before a suppressed line only in flagLine (see the svFlags finding) and on error-only logOnce / hudLog paths.
kept.fix: No change to the Lua logger. A buffered writer would save under 0.05 ms a tick and would lose the last lines on a crash; the Lua log exists because UE4SS.log loses its tail on a crash. Spend the effort on the native flush and SV_LogUnits instead. Crash breadcrumbs stay as they are (immediate).
kept.gameplay_note: No change proposed.
kept.risk: None

verify.cost_check: sv_core.lua:44-56: `local ok, f = pcall(io.open, dir .. "AC8SurvivalMode_lua.log", "w")`, `f:setvbuf("no")`, and log() does `print(TAG .. s .. "\n")` plus one `LOG_FILE:write(os.date("%H:%M:%S ") .. s .. "\n")`. That is one WriteFile per line with no FlushFileBuffers. crumb() (line 59) calls native Crumb, which only does WriteFile (survival_rt.c 199). UE4SS.log timestamps show consecutive Survival lines 31-44 µs apart (e.g. 13:22:23.5550453 to .5551811 to .5552933). The per-tick average is negligible next to the native flush (finding 0) and the walks.
verify.gameplay_check: No change is proposed.
verify.safety_check: Keeping the write-through Lua log preserves its purpose (UE4SS.log loses its tail on a crash). A buffered writer would lose exactly those lines.
verify.refined_fix: No change. Optional cosmetic: hoist the per-call closure in log() (`local function put(s) LOG_FILE:write(...) end`, then pcall(put, s)) to save a tiny allocation per line. Not worth a build on its own.
verify.est_saving: None (under 0.05 ms a tick available).
